newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Senior Slovak bishop warns PM to respect citizens.
newsitem.headline: Senior Slovak bishop warns PM to respect citizens.

text.p: Slovakia's powerful Roman Catholic church has joined the country's opposition, actors and students in a protest against government policies, warning Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's administration to respect citizens' rights.

"I support trade unions, representatives of culture, actors, students, and all other citizens who demand a dialogue with the ruling political power and the restoration of respect by the government for citizens," the independent daily Pravda quoted Rudolf Balaz, head of the Bishops' Conference, as saying.

Balaz called for the ruling coalition, consisting of the Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS), the ultra-right Slovak National Party (SNS) and the extreme-left Workers Party (ZRS), to change their way of governing the country.

The government, in a statement, rejected Balaz's arguments, saying it was "unusual that a high representative of the Catholic church called for citizens to protest against the government elected in democratic elections."
Many theatres, including the National Theatre, began striking last month to protest what actors consider to be increasing state interference in their artistic management.
Actors and opposition parties have demanded the dismissal of Culture Minister Ivan Hudec for what they say is his incompetent management of the cultural sector.
Earlier this week, university students joined the protest calling for Hudec's dismissal and annoucning a strike alert.
Government officials, including Meciar, have rejected the protesters' demands, saying the actors and students are being manipulated by the opposition which is trying to seize power.

The Bishops' Conference, in a country where more than half of the population are registerd Catholics, has several times expressed concerns over Meciar's policies. Balaz has also accused the security service (SIS) of attempts to discredit him.
